pr_title: posix: eventfd: fix read deadlock and add test coverage
pr_body:
7 commits (please see each commit message for details)

* tests: posix: eventfd: use reopen in test_write_then_read (should have gone into #58406)
* lib: os: add `k_condvar` for each fdtable entry
* posix: eventfd: un-inline `eventfd_read()` and `eventfd_write()`
* posix: eventfd: revise locking, signaling, and allocation
* tests: posix: eventfd: blocking read-write test for deadlock bug
* posix: eventfd: deprecate non-public EFD macros
* tests: posix: eventfd: add stress test

Fixes #58426

Note: this improves non-blocking `eventfd` performance significantly.

I would suggest reading each commit individually with the exception of the eventfd revision.

For that one, it's probably easiest just to look at the end result [here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/5d67c8a8037d0c6b974cdc45ae2e779fae8a5c42/lib/posix/eventfd.c).
pr_comments: * added Meta copyright since `lib/posix/eventfd.c` was more or less a complete rewrite

Marking `DNM` for today.

I'm going to do another respin of this with special consideration given to the case where `O_NONBLOCK` is specified, but also taking into account some of the potential race conditions that could occur between threads attempting to access the same file descriptor - e.g. `poll()` vs `close()`.

It occurred to me, that I've opened the possibility that `eventfd_read()` and `eventfd_write()` could be used from interrupt context.

issue_context.title: posix: eventfd: deadlock on blocking read

review_comments:
How safe is it to allow a caller defined function to be called while holding the spin lock?

I guess it is somewhat moot since it is clearly necessary to lock here. Just asking for curiosity.
This function is static and the only functions that are being passed in are `eventfd_read_locked()` and `eventfd_wrote_locked()`
nit: while waiting of a condition variable maybe would be better?
The mutex is taken as part of waiting on the condition variable. Same same
z_ is reserved for private functions and calls, this header is full of z_ call and it is a public API, we need to fix this at some point.

>  header is full of z_ call and it is a public API, we need to fix this at some point. 

@nashif - what do you think of "zvfs" or "zfdio"?

I think these next few lines of code could lead to one of the classic examples for deadlock 

t1: unlock(a) lock(b) lock(a)

and if another thread tries to acquire both locks then:
t2: lock(a) lock(b)
= deadlock

Is this scenario possible here? 

That said I think it is clear that you have to give up the spin lock before trying to lock the mutex. Just curious if the scenario is possible.

> Is this scenario possible here? 

I can see why you might think that based on your earlier question.

Since `op()` is only either `eventfd_read_locked()` or 
`eventfd_write_locked()` any threads executing those functions will never be stalled on anything, so you can ignore the inner spin lock / unlock.


What you're left with is just the outer mutex lock / unlock, which is business as usual.
Is this superfluous? Does it have to be -1 can you just return ret?

The return value needs to be either 0 or -1, but `ret` will be either `sizeof(eventfd_t)` or -1.

The reason that `ret` couldn't just be zero is to also support the regular `write()` and `read()` calls (i.e. non-eventfd / POSIX versions).

Technically, I could have made a comparison against 0 as well, I just tend to prefer branching on the error case.
